newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE SNEAK HOME WITH LATE TRIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE SNEAK HOME WITH LATE TRIES.

text.p: Two tries in the last six minutes saved France from a third successive defeat at Cardiff Arms Park on Wednesday as they scrambled to a 40-33 success over Wales in a friendly international.

Experienced forward Abdel Benazzi and 22-year-old centre Stephane Glas, with his second try of the match, both dived over under the posts in the closing minutes for converted scores to secure a win which had looked remote when they trailed 27-10 at halftime.
The home side had scored three good tries to lead 27-10 at the interval, but were unable to hold on after seeing both captain Nigel Davies and former skipper Ieuan Evans stretchered off.

French centre Richard Dourthe kicked four conversions and four penalties but was involved in at least two nasty off-the- ball incidents as the visiting side grew frustrated with Canadian referee George Gadjovich.
The match may have been billed as a friendly but the opening 20 minutes' action made that description look absurd.
France, who eventually decided to award caps on the flight across the channel, encountered a Welsh side in no mood to offer gifts and were a try down inside the first two minutes.
Wales's inexperienced pack made a roaring start and hooker Barry Williams barged over for one of the quickest tries ever scored by a player on his international debut.

Evans sprinted over for a second try to reward some sparkling handling after only eight minutes as France struggled to find any sort of momentum in a game which quickly developed into a physical contest.

The departure of Davies and Evans, who suffered a gashed thigh in preventing his opposite number Philippe Saint-Andre from scoring in the corner, crucially left Wales short of their two most experienced three-quarters and forced tiny fly-half Arwel Thomas to play out of position on the wing.

Glas took advantage by sidestepping through the disorganised Welsh defence for his first score, but Gareth Thomas swiftly gathered a chip from Jenkins to reopen the gap, assisted by Jenkins's trusty boot.
The fly-half kicked 18 points in total and saw another bounce away off the cross-bar, but although his side led until the 74th minute they could not complete the job.
Jean-Luc Sadourny, after more good work from Glas, dragged France back to 27-20 in the 50th minute as France put aside their dissatisfaction with the referee and applied themselves to the rugby.
They were a little fortunate in the end, but both sides learned plenty as they prepare to welcome world champions South Africa to Europe.
